catalog_quote: Maurer 2013 (APiCS ch. 36, Phonology): "The tonal system of Angolar is not fully investigated, yet a preliminary analysis of disyllabic nouns in subject position followed by a disyllabic verb modified by the future marker ka shows that there exist four different tone melodies (HH, HL, LH, LL), which points to a two-tone system (own fieldwork, 2008): (1) áwá ká gàʃtà 'The water will be wasted.' ... fóθà ká kàbà 'The energy will come to an end.' ... kàθó ká pèndè 'The dog will get lost.' ... The syllable structure is of the (C)V type; up to four syllables are possible: a-dha 'wing', ne-ne-ka 'to endanger', or ma-ra-ka-tho 'demarcation'." Bandeira, Agostinho & Freitas 2021, fn. 4: "Em relação ao angolar, Maurer (1995) e Lorenzino (1998) propõem que o angolar apresenta tom lexical, mas não apresentam uma análise fonológica aprofundada. Neste trabalho, não abordaremos a descrição do sistema …

audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: Quote check: both deciding quotations are verbatim in the copies we hold at the stated places. The classification tonal rests on a 2013 APiCS grammar sketch by the principal fieldworker (own 2008 data), and the APiCS Tone datapoint 36-120 downloaded now independently codes Angolar 'Simple tone system, for lexical and grammatical distinctions' with Confidence: Certain, so the record faithfully reports the only committed analysis in the literature. It is not 'well-sourced' because (a) Maurer himself calls the analysis preliminary and says his 1995 treatment 'has to be seriously amended'; (b) neither full grammar (Maurer 1995, Lorenzino 1998) is. (c) a competing reading exists: Bandeira 2017 (pp. 259–260, 313; held by the project under saot1239, read now) treats Angolar as having primary stress on the final, penultimate or antepenultimate syllable and remarks that Maurer's tone examples look like tone 'confundid
audit.second_reader_evidence: The quotation was checked again: re-done independently. (1) Maurer 2013 APiCS survey ch. 36 'Phonology' — the deciding quotation is verbatim in lines 133-151 ('The tonal system of Angolar is not fully investigated, yet a preliminary analysis of disyllabic nouns.. four different tone melodies (HH, HL, LH, LL), which points to a two-tone system (own fieldwork, 2008)'; examples áwá ká gàʃtà / fóθà ká kàbà / kàθó ká pèndè / àlè ká pɛ̀nθà; 'Tonal distinctions are also used in order to differentiate syntactic categories.. ðùrà 'to help' vs. ðúrá 'help''; the (C)V / ma-ra-ka-tho syllable sentence at line 2

sources.quote: p. 259–260: 'Quanto ao angolar, pouco se sabe sobre o suposto sistema tonal defendido por Maurer (1995) ... Para o angolar, Maurer (1995: 9) propõe dois tons: H e L ... HH (mámá ["mama] ‘seio’), LL (màmà [ma"ma] ‘amamentar’), HL (mótxì ["mOti] ‘morte’) e LH (bòbó [bO"bO] ‘maduro’) ... Os exemplos, mencionados por Maurer (1995), assemelham-se com o ocorrido em santome, em que o tom é confundido com o acento primário.' p. 313: 'Em santome, fa d’ambô, lung’i e angolar, o acento pode ser atribuído à última, penúltima ou antepenúltima sílaba', Angolar: final [Te"kwa] ‘percevejo’, prefinal ["fesu] ‘
